Further, we showcase the benefits of the proposed approach compared to existing methods in numerical examples. We note that the existing methods in [20], [21] also used SOS optimization to control bilinear systems. However, these approaches only address nominal bilinear systems, whereas we propose a robust controller design which can cope with the uncertainty due to the Koopman operator approximation.

The paper is organized as follows. In Section II, we introduce the considered class of nonlinear systems and the corresponding data-driven system representation based on SafedMD. Then, in Section III, we first present the proposed SOS-based controller design for the special case of bilinear systems with known system dynamics to ease the exposition.

The general case of data-driven control for unknown nonlinear systems is addressed in Section IV. Finally, we illustrate the proposed approach in numerical examples in Section V, before concluding the paper in Section VI.

Notation: We write $I_p$ for the $p \times p$ identity matrix and $0_{p \times q}$ for the $p \times q$ zero matrix, where we omit the index if the dimension is clear from the context. A vector of ones is denoted by $\mathbb{1}_d \in \mathbb{R}^d$. For symmetric $A$, we write $A \succ 0$ or $A \succeq 0$ if $A$ is positive definite or positive semidefinite, respectively. Negative (semi)definiteness is defined analogously. Matrix blocks which can be inferred from symmetry are denoted by $*$ and we abbreviate $B^\top AB$ by writing $[*]^{\top} AB$. The Kronecker product is denoted by $\otimes$. Further, we denote by $\mathbb{R}[x,d]$ the set of all polynomials $s$ in the variable $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with degree $d$ and real coefficients, i.e., $s(x) = \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}_0^n, |\alpha| \leq d} s_\alpha x^\alpha$ with $s_\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ and $|\alpha| \leq d \in \mathbb{N}_0$. Here, $x^\alpha = x_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots x_n^{\alpha_n}$ are monomials for a vectorial index $\alpha \in \mathbb{N}_0^n$, where $|\alpha| = \alpha_1 + \cdots + \alpha_n$. The set of all $p \times q$-matrices with elements in $\mathbb{R}[x,d]$ is denoted by $\mathbb{R}[x,d]^{p \times q}$. If a matrix $S \in \mathbb{R}[x,2d]^{p \times p}$ can be decomposed as $S = T^\top T$ for some $T \in \mathbb{R}[x,d]^{q \times p}$, then $S$ is called an SOS matrix in $x$ and we write $S \in \text{SOS}[x,2d]^p$. Finally, we say $S \in \mathbb{R}[x,2d]^{p \times p}$ is strictly SOS if $(S - \varepsilon I_p) \in \text{SOS}[x,2d]^p$ for some $\varepsilon > 0$, denoted by $S \in \text{SOS}_+[x,2d]^p$.

III. PROBLEM SETTING

We consider unknown nonlinear control-affine systems of the form
$x(t) = f_c(x(t), u(t)) = f(x(t)) + \sum_{i=1}^{m} g_i(x(t)) u_i(t)$ (I)
with state $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, input $u \in \mathbb{R}^m$, initial condition $x(0) \in \mathbb{R}^n$, and unknown functions $f$ and $g_i$, $i \in 1, ..., m$. Further, we assume that $f(0) = 0$ holds, i.e., that the origin is a controlled equilibrium for $u = 0$.

**Assumption 1.** The vector field $f_c : \mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^n$ is continuous and locally Lipschitz in its first argument around the origin.

Assumption 1 is satisfied for many practical systems and ensures a smooth behavior between sampled data points. The goal of this paper is to design a state-feedback controller $u = \mu(x)$ for the unknown nonlinear system (I) that is guaranteed to stabilize the origin of the system. To this end, we first find a suitable data-driven system representation, for which we leverage Koopman operator theory and its finite-dimensional approximation. More precisely, we rely on SafEDMD [17] which uses a lifted bilinear representation of system (I) with the lifted state $\Phi(x) = [x^\top \phi_{n+1} \cdots \phi_N]^\top$ and the corresponding (discrete-time) dynamics
\[\Phi(x_{k+1}) = A\Phi(x_k) + B_0 u_k + \tilde{B}(u_k \otimes \Phi(x_k)) + r(x_k, u_k) \tag{2}\]
with $x_k = x(k\Delta t)$ for some sampling rate $\Delta t > 0$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}_0$. Here, the system matrices $A, B_0, \tilde{B}$ are estimated by data samples from repeated experiments with different constant inputs $u(t) \equiv \bar{u}$, i.e., we consider the dataset
\[\mathcal{D} = \{ (x^\bar{u}(t_j), x^{\bar{u}}(t_j + \Delta t)) \}_{j=1}^{\bar{t}} \text{ for } \bar{u} \in \{0, e_1, ..., e_m\} 
\tag{3}\]
with unit vectors $e_i \in \mathbb{R}^m$. Based on the data $\mathcal{D}$, we define
\[\Phi_X^\bar{u} = 
\begin{bmatrix}
\Phi(x^\bar{u}(t_1)) & \cdots & \Phi(x^\bar{u}(t_d))
\end{bmatrix} 
, 
\Phi_{X+}^\bar{u} = 
\begin{bmatrix}
\Phi(x^\bar{u}(t_1 + \Delta t)) & \cdots & \Phi(x^\bar{u}(t_d + \Delta t)) 
\end{bmatrix},
\text{ and solve the linear regression problems}
A = \arg \min_{(A \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n})} \| \Phi_X^k - A \Phi_X^0 \|_F , 
(B_0, i, B_i) = \arg \min_{(B_0,i, B_i \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n})} \| \Phi_{X+}^e - [B_0,i, B_i] \|_F , 
\tag{4b}\]
Then, we stack the matrices $B_{0,i}, B_i$ and define $B_0 = [B_{0,1} \cdots B_{0,m}]$ and $\tilde{B} = [B_1 - A  \cdots  B_m - A]$. Further, the residual can be proven to satisfy the proportional bound
\[\| r(x,u) \| \leq c_x \| \Phi(x) \| + c_u \| u \| 
\tag{5}\]
for some $c_x, c_u > 0$, see [17, Cor. 3.2] for details.

III. SOS-BASED CONTROLLER DESIGN FOR BILINEAR SYSTEMS

Next, we propose a rational state-feedback controller based on SOS optimization. To this end, we first restrict ourselves to discrete-time bilinear systems, i.e., system (2) with $\Phi(x) = x$ leading to
\[x_+ = Ax + B_0 u + \tilde{B}(u \otimes x) + r(x, u), 
\tag{6}\]

where for brevity we write $(x_+, x, u)$ for $(x_{k+1}, x_k, u_k)$. In this section, we assume that the system matrices $A, B_0, \tilde{B}$ are known and that the proportional bound
\[\| r(x, u) \| \leq c_x \| x \| + c_u \| u \| 
\tag{7}\]

on the unknown residual $r(x, u)$ holds true. As shown in [21, Prop. 3, Prop. 4], an unstable discrete-time bilinear system can only be (globally) stabilized by a rational control law if the degrees of the polynomial in the numerator and the polynomial in the denominator are the same. Hence, neither a linear nor a polynomial state feedback is sufficient to stabilize the bilinear system.

Next, we derive the closed-loop dynamics of the feedback controller design as well as derive the resulting bilinear stabilizing decoupled state-feedback pair of the scalar piece-wise feedback controller.

### IV. KOOPMAN-BASED CONTROL VIA SOS OPTIMIZATION  

After establishing a guaranteed stabilizing controller design for bilinear systems, we now extend the results of Section III to general nonlinear systems (1) using Koopman operator theory. To this end, we rely on the data-driven bilinear surrogate model (2) obtained by SasEDMD. Then, we design a state- feedback controller \(\mu (x)\) analogous to the bilinear case in Theorem 2 to stabilize the origin of the nonlinear system (1). Here, \(\mu (x)\) is rational in the lifted state \(\Phi (x)\). Before stating the main result, we introduce an assumption on the data-driven bilinear surrogate model.

Suppose the bilinear surrogate model (2) is obtained via SasEDMD with some \(\Delta t > 0\) and data \(\mathcal{D}\) in (3) sampled i.i.d. from a compact region \(\mathbb{X}\) for some data length \(d > 0\) , and the projection error onto the finite-dimensional dictionary spanned by the observable function \(\Phi\) is proportionally bounded with constants \(\tilde{c}_x\) , \(\tilde{c}_u\) , e.g., trivially due to the invariance of the dictionary. Then, Assumption 3 is satisfied for \(c_x = \tilde{c}_x + \bar{c}_x\) and \(c_u = \tilde{c}_u + \bar{c}_u\) with probability \(1 - \delta \in (0,1)\) due to [17, Cor. 3.2], where \(\bar{c}_x, \bar{c}_u \in O(1 / \sqrt{\delta d} + \Delta t^2)\) . For a more detailed discussion on how to establish a proportional bound on the projection error, we refer to [26]. The following corollary establishes our proposed data-driven controller design for nonlinear systems.  

Corollary 4. Suppose Assumptions 1 and 3 hold. If there exist \(\alpha >0\) , \(P = P^\top >0\) of size \(N \times N\) , \(L_n \in \mathbb{R}[\mathtt{z},2\alpha -1]^{i \times N}\) , \(\tau \in \text{SOS}_{+}[z,2\alpha ]\) , \(u_d \in \text{SOS}_{+}[z, 2\alpha ]\) , and \(\rho > 0\) such that (16) holds with \(z \in \mathbb{R}^N\) , then the sampled controller  

\[\mu_{\mathrm{s}}(x(t)) = \mu (x(k\Delta t)),\quad t\in [k\Delta t,(k + 1)\Delta t),k\geq 0 \quad (17)\]  

with \(\begin{array}{r}\mu (x) = \frac{1}{u_d(\Phi(x))} L_n(\Phi (x))P^{- 1}\Phi (x) \end{array}\) globally exponentially stabilizes the origin of the continuous-time nonlinear system (1).  

Proof. See [17], [25] for the necessary modifications in the proof of Theorem 2, and we refer to [17, Cor. 4.2] to derive the closed- loop stability of the continuous- time system based on sampled feedback.  

Corollary 4 provides a guaranteed stabilizing controller for the unknown nonlinear system (1) based on the bilinear surrogate model (2) obtained by SasEDMD. More precisely, the sampled nonlinear feedback controller (17) is determined by solving the SOS program (16) for a fixed \(u_d\) , which serves as an additional degree of freedom chosen by the user. Next, we apply Corollary 4 to control an unknown nonlinear system. We consider the well-studied nonlinear inverted pendulum (see [2] and the reference therein) with the continuous-time dynamics

#### x1=x2,
x2=gbsin(x1)-bm/2x_2+ml/2 * u.

For the simulation, we choose $m = 1, l = 1, b = 0.5, g = 9.81, but assume the system dynamics to be unknown except for a dataset of input-state measurements as in (3). To this end, for each constant input $u \equiv \bar{u} \in \{0,1\}$ we collect $d = 200$ data pairs $(x,x_+)$ with $x$ i.i.d. sampled from $\mathbb{X} = [-\pi,\pi]^2$. Then, we define the lifting function $\Phi(x) = \begin{bmatrix}x_1 & x_2 & \sin(x_1) \end{bmatrix}^\top$ and apply SafeDDM to generate a discrete-time bilinear surrogate model by solving the linear regression problem (4). For the residual $r$, we consider Assumption 3 with the constants $c_x = 1 \cdot 10^{-2}$ and $c_u = 1 \cdot 10^{-3}$ for the proportional bond (5). Then, we follow Corollary 4 to design an SOS-based rational controller in the lifted state $\Phi(x)$ stabilizing the underlying nonlinear system. For the controller design, we choose the denominator by including all monomials in $\mathbb{R}[\Phi(x), 2]$, i.e.,

u_d $

= 1 + x_1^2 + x_1^2 + x_2^2 + x_1 \sin(x_1) + x_2 \sin(x_1) + \sin(x_1)^2,

where $u_d$ can be easily verified to be strictly SOS, i.e., $u_d \in \text{SOS}_+[\Phi(x), 2]$. Fig. 2 depicts the guaranteed RoA of the proposed SOS-based controller design for the unknown nonlinear system, where we maximized the volume of the Lyapunov sublevel set $\Omega$ in the SOS program.

Further, we emphasize that most of the existing methods lack closed-loop guarantees for the underlying nonlinear system. We compare our method to [17] which in turn was compared extensively to Koopman-based control methods that do not provide closed-loop guarantees (like EDMDc [33]) and therefore fail. In particular, we compare the resulting guaranteed RoA to the RoA of the Koopman-based controller design [17, Cor. 4.2], which relies on solving LMIs by over-approximating the bilinearity of the surrogate model. We note that the LMI-based controller design is not feasible for the chosen constants $c_x$, $c_u$ with the data length $d$ and, thus, cannot guarantee closed-loop stability of the nonlinear system based on the collected dataset. Instead, we solve the controller design of [17] with the smaller constants $c_x = 2 \cdot 10^{-3}, c_u = 2 \cdot 10^{-4}$, and over-approximate the bilinearity within the ellipsoidal region $\|\Phi(x)\|^2 \leq 0.01$. As seen in Fig. 2, the LMI-based controller design yields a significantly smaller RoA compared to the proposed SOS-based controller design. Thus, the proposed SOS-based controller design outperforms the existing approach by providing a guaranteed stabilizing controller for the unknown nonlinear system within a significantly larger RoA and based on a smaller dataset, showing the improved robustness w.r.t. the uncertainty in the bilinear surrogate model.
